    Plot changes in predicted values relative to a threshold

    plot_prediction_change.Rd

    Produces a scatter plot comparing original and updated prediction values, with colour highlighting based either on whether predictions cross a threshold or on supplied observation values. A prediction is considered to have changed if it is greater than or equal to threshold in pred_original and below threshold in pred_new. Optionally prints the rows corresponding to such changes.

    plot_prediction_change(
  pred_original,
  pred_new,
  threshold,
  obs_vals = NULL,
  print_change = TRUE,
  col_by = "pred_change",
  x_lab = "Original predictions",
  y_lab = "New predictions",
  title = "Prediction change"
)

    Arguments

    pred_original

    Numeric vector of original prediction values.

    pred_new

    Numeric vector of updated prediction values.

    threshold

    Single numeric threshold used to identify prediction changes.

    obs_vals

    Optional numeric vector of observation values used for colouring when col_by = "obs_vals". Must be the same length as pred_original.

    print_change

    Logical; if TRUE, prints rows where predictions cross the threshold from above to below. Defaults to TRUE.

    col_by

    Character string indicating the variable used for colour: "pred_change" (default) colours points by threshold crossing, whereas "obs_vals" colours points using obs_vals.

    x_lab

    Character string for the x-axis label. Defaults to "Original predictions".

    y_lab

    Character string for the y-axis label. Defaults to "New predictions".

    title

    Character string for the plot title. Defaults to "Prediction change".

    Value

    A ggplot2 object showing original vs. new predictions.

    Details

    When col_by = "pred_change", points are coloured according to whether they cross the threshold. When col_by = "obs_vals", the supplied observation values determine the colouring instead. The diagonal reference line is added to help visualise deviations between original and new predictions.

    Examples

    if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
plot_prediction_change(
  pred_original = c(-3, -1, 0, 2),
  pred_new = c(-4, -2, -0.5, 1.5),
  threshold = 0,
  col_by = "pred_change"
)
} # }
